Outlet: GOV.UK (Prime Minister's Office, 10 Downing Street), published 12 October 2026 (NOTE: background — summit date confirmation; not new this weekend)

Prime Minister to attend UK-EU summit in Brussels on 20 November

The Prime Minister will convene with António Costa, President of the European Council, and Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, in Brussels on 20 November 2026 for the second UK-EU summit.

The Prime Minister intends to leverage the summit to advance agreements aimed at reducing expenses and regulatory burdens for British farmers and businesses, bolstering industry, and fostering expansion across all regions of the country.

During the inaugural summit held in London on 19 May 2025, the UK and EU established a fresh strategic partnership.

In Brussels, leaders will assess advancements since that meeting and determine concrete measures to strengthen cooperation on security, illegal migration and crime, while diminishing red tape and decreasing costs for farmers and food businesses.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated: "A threadbare Brexit deal has damaged our economy. Britain can do so much better, so at this summit I want to take practical steps that pay off for the British public, cutting costs for our farmers, food producers and families."

He continued: "The EU is our closest neighbour, largest market and a vital security partner."
